subject: Spatio-temporal models for monthly temperatures, problems with AR1 model

messages.author: 7a4a5fe753932e1a
messages.subject: Spatio-temporal models for monthly temperatures, problems with AR1 model
parts:
Hi,

I am working on a spatio-temporal model for the interpolation of monthly temperatures in Italy, using a dataset of 144 point stations/time series covering 58 years (1961-2018).

The model is very simple:

 temp~0+Intercept+sdem+sdis_costa+yy+f(i,model=spde, group=i.group,control.group=list(model="ar1")) #MODEL 1

with sdem (standardized station elevation), sdis_costa (standardized distance from the coast) and yy (year, ranging between 1961 and 2018).

The temporal index varies between 1 and 696 (58 years x 12 months).

The mesh was generated without the use of a shapefile (despite the Italian coast be visible in the attached image):

 as_Spatial(s.utm.ana)->sp.utm.ana

 inla.nonconvex.hull(points=sp.utm.ana)->italiaInla #no shapefile

 inla.mesh.2d(boundary = italiaInla,cutoff = 8000,max.edge = c(40000),offset =c(200000),min.angle =21)->mesh

As a first approach, I have not considered the presence of the sea between the Italian Peninsula and its islands.

Unfortunately using such a model, the latent field shows unreasonable values (values higher than 400!). The model fits very well the training dataset but, for the validation dataset, a limited set of stations shows very high RMSE values. Finally, the model exhibits a PIT values distribution far from the uniform.

After a lot of trials I identified this model (MODEL 2):

 list(theta = list(prior="pc.prec", param=c(1,0.01)))->hyper.list
 temp~0+Intercept+sdem+sdis_costa+yy+f(mm,model="rw1",hyper=hyper.list)+f(i,model=spde, group=i.group,control.group=list(model="iid"))  #mm: month of the year: 1,2 ..12  #

With this model, the above-said problems disappear (almost uniform PIT values distribution, low RMSE values in the validation and training phases, reasonable latent field values). The interpolated temperature maps produced through this model are comparable with the maps produced through a simpler regression kriging approach (only spatial, using gstat package).

The problem seems to be connected with the AR1 model in the control.group, causing data overfitting.

As suggested in many posts, I tried a further approach (MODEL 3): PC priors for both the AR1 model and the spde

inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh,prior.range=c(200000,0.2),prior.sigma=c(5,0.1),alpha=2)->spde              #CRS, epsg:32632/coordinates in meters

temp~0+Intercept+sdem+sdis_costa+yy+f(i,model=spde, group=i.group,control.group=list(model="ar1",hyper=list(theta=list(prior='pc.cor1', param=c(0.7, 0.8)))))

Actually, the use of PC priors improves the latent field, but its values are still too high than expected (SEE attached image). Some stations still show fitting problems in the validation phase (see the fitted vs observed values scatterplot) and the PIT distribution is not good (see image).

I would appreciate a suggestion on what I am doing wrong. I have spent a lot of time doing several trials on the mesh resolution, priors for the fixed effects but I cannot solve the problem with the AR1 model.


Thanks in advance
Guido

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Spatio-temporal models for monthly temperatures, problems with AR1 model
parts:
Hi Guido,

"wrong" can be many different types of problems.

One is coding. This you can check by fixing the hyperparameter in the ar1 to give a rho close to 0. This should reproduce the iid group model.

One is whether your measures of fit are good. In the third figure, you do a spline regression wrt the x axis. What if you instead do a spline regression wrt the y=x axis? If you think of it this way, it seems the model has three types of points: good, biased up, and biased down.

A third type of "wrong" is whether the model is a good model for the data or not. This is very hard to know... no model is correct etc. In space-time models, I think it is common to find some mismatch between the model and the data. What if you reconsider the data as time-series with some spatial structure? Plot the time series and see if there are any patterns that jump out at you. Are there any time-series artifacts? E.g. are there any change in measurement conditions that result in jumps in the time series?

Best,
Haakon

parts:
Hi Guido,

Some further things to consider:
The effect of “distance to coast” is highly unlikely to be linear.
Measuring distances in metres when working on the scale of an entire country is virtually certain to lead to numerical floating point problems. I highly recommend converting UTM coordinates to kilometres.

Finn

parts:
Thanks a lot for your attention and suggestions.
